messages.text: Our dad died and left the house in his will. My sister A wants to buy it with her husband at a "family discount". I'm not signing off on that. Our younger sister B could use some money too. Can you help us sort this out?

I want the will followed and my financial share treated fairly. If A wants to buy the house, I won’t subsidize a discounted price; we need to agree on a fair valuation and terms first. And yes—no one should be pressured to sign.

I’d like to buy the house with my husband, ideally at a family discount. I want a clear plan, but I know C hasn’t agreed, so we can’t proceed without her. I’m not sure what price or shares would be fair yet, and I’m concerned that leaving things unresolved could strain us further.

Thank you. What matters most to me is having some money to start a dance studio. I’m not sure the house has to be sold if there’s another fair way for me to receive that money, but the amount and arrangements would need to be discussed.

An independent appraisal is fine, provided we agree on the appraiser and method first. I can’t state the will’s terms without seeing them; let’s share the actual document. I’m not in a hurry, so we can set a check-in date, but not a deadline that pressures anyone to decide.

I’m willing to use an independent appraisal as a reference, but I’m not agreeing in advance to pay the full appraised value; I’m hoping for a family discount. I can’t give a reliable budget or closing date yet. I don’t have the will’s terms in front of me, so I can’t confirm the shares or conditions.

I don’t have a reliable studio budget or start date yet, so I can’t give you a useful number; I’ll need to work that out. I’d be open to an independent appraisal as a way to establish value, though it wouldn’t settle the other terms. I don’t know the will’s exact wording, so I can’t confirm its shares or conditions.
Item 11 is fair in principle, but don’t assume how the discount would affect each share until we’ve seen the will and agreed the terms. I don’t know who has the will.
I don’t know who has the will. I can ask around, but I can’t share its terms yet. I don’t have a reliable price range until I’ve reviewed the will and talked it through with my husband.
I’m afraid I don’t know who has the will. Perhaps the executor or your father’s lawyer can tell us and arrange a copy for all three of us.
I’ll check Dad’s papers at home. A two-week check-in is fine if it’s just to report back, not pressure anyone to decide.
I can ask around the family about who may have the will. A check-in in about two weeks sounds fine; we’ll need to agree on a time together. I’d rather choose an appraiser after we have the will.
I can try contacting any solicitor or bank connected with Dad, though I’m not sure who they were. A check-in in about two weeks is fine; please suggest a day and time.
Yes, add it: if the searches turn up nothing, we can ask a solicitor to help find the will. We can agree on any costs before committing.
Yes, add item 12. If the searches turn up nothing, we should discuss asking a solicitor to search; the cost and who would cover it still need to be agreed.
Yes, that seems sensible—if these searches turn up nothing, we should ask a solicitor to help trace the will.
